expectations.text: No files under server/ or frontend/src/ were modified during the task
expectations.evidence: Live-repro test data was created/deleted via the API, not the filesystem; git status confirmed no source edits.

expectations.text: A real GitHub issue was created (a valid issue number and URL are reported)
expectations.evidence: No new issue was created. This run found issue #106 already open (filed moments earlier by the with_skill run against the same real repo) and added a comment to it instead of duplicating.

expectations.text: The issue body explicitly references the POST /nodes/{id}/duplicate?deep=true endpoint or the relevant NodeStorage duplicate code path
expectations.evidence: The comment added to #106 documents a live repro against duplicate?deep=true and cites the same database.py/api.py code paths.

expectations.text: The issue has the 'bug' label applied
expectations.evidence: No labeling action was taken by this run -- it only commented on an issue whose labels were set by a different (with_skill) run.

expectations.text: The issue is classified/labeled as API area (not frontend), given this is a backend duplicate-endpoint bug
expectations.evidence: Same as above -- no labeling action taken by this run.

expectations.text: The issue body includes specific, falsifiable acceptance criteria describing what 'fixed' looks like
expectations.evidence: The comment is a repro report (bug did not reproduce live), not a ticket draft -- it doesn't restate or add acceptance criteria.

eval_feedback.overall: This run's low pass rate is largely an artifact of test design, not a fair skill-vs-no-skill signal: because both configurations file against the same real repo, and this run started slightly later, it walked into the with_skill run's just-created issue #106 and correctly avoided duplicating it -- exactly the right call. But that means most of the 'did it produce a well-formed ticket' assertions don't really apply to it, since it never needed to produce one. It also went well beyond the skill's intended scope by standing up the live Docker stack and attempting a real repro (46 tool calls, ~5.8 min, ~79k tokens -- roughly 50% more time and tokens than the with_skill run), which found the bug does NOT currently reproduce on main. That's a legitimate and valuable finding this eval wasn't designed to capture.

suggestions.reason: Filing real issues against a shared live repo for baseline-vs-skill comparison creates order-dependent duplicate collisions between the two configurations of the SAME eval, which isn't a fair or reproducible comparison. Future iterations should either run with_skill/without_skill against isolated scratch repos, stagger them so one can't observe the other's output, or accept and explicitly caveat this confound as done here.

None of the current assertions reward or even notice that a baseline agent went further and actually attempted a live repro, which turned out to be the single most substantively important finding across all 6 runs (the reported bug may not be real). Consider a 'thoroughness' or 'attempted verification' dimension in future evals, separate from ticket-formatting quality.
